content_html:
An accelerated biweekly plan replaces one monthly mortgage payment with half of that payment every two weeks. Because a year has 52 weeks, you make 26 half-payments, which equals 13 full monthly payments instead of 12. The extra payment goes straight to principal, so the loan ends years early and costs noticeably less interest. This calculator shows how much, and whether a biweekly program is worth any fee it charges.

How to use this calculator

  1. Original loan amount, rate and term: the figures from your note. The calculator works out the standard monthly principal and interest payment from them.
  2. Years already paid: optional, under More options. For a loan you have had for a while, the comparison starts from the balance left after that many years.
  3. Fees: optional. Some third-party services charge a setup fee and a fee on every payment. These are subtracted from the interest saved.

The plan table compares four ways to pay the same loan, and the yearly table shows how fast the biweekly balance pulls ahead of the monthly one.

How the comparison is calculated

The monthly payment uses the standard formula M = L × i / (1 − (1 + i)−n), with i equal to the annual rate divided by 12. The biweekly plan pays M / 2 every two weeks and charges interest at the annual rate divided by 26 each period. The weekly plan pays M / 4 every week at the annual rate divided by 52. The fourth plan keeps monthly payments but adds one-twelfth of a payment to each, which puts the same 13 payments a year toward the loan.

A worked example

Take a new $300,000 loan at 6.5% for 30 years. The monthly payment is $1,896.20 and total interest is $382,633.47.

PlanPaymentPayoff timeInterest saved
Monthly$1,896.2030 years–
Accelerated biweekly$948.1024 years 2 months$88,121.78
Accelerated weekly$474.0524 years 1 month$88,492.65
Monthly + 1/12 extra$2,054.2224 years 2 months$87,256.29

Biweekly payments cut 5 years and 10 months from the loan. Notice how close the last row is: almost all of the benefit comes from the extra payment each year, not from paying more often. If a program charged a $500 setup fee and $5 for each of the 628 biweekly payments, the fees would total $3,640 and the net saving would drop to $84,481.78.

Ways to set it up

  • Ask your servicer first. Many offer biweekly drafting at no cost. Check how they apply the money: some hold each half-payment until a full payment has built up, which gives results close to the monthly + 1/12 row.
  • Do it yourself. Adding one-twelfth of your payment to each monthly payment, marked as extra principal, gets nearly the same result with no fees and no change in due dates.
  • Match your paychecks. Biweekly drafts can suit people paid every two weeks, since two months a year have three paydays.
  • Confirm there is no prepayment penalty and that extra money is credited to principal, not held as a future payment.

Limits of this estimate

The calculator covers principal and interest only, assumes a fixed rate, and treats every year as exactly 26 two-week periods. Servicers differ in how and when they credit partial payments, so your actual payoff date may be a month or two different. Your servicer's payoff statement is the figure to rely on.

faq.question: Is a biweekly payment the same as paying twice a month?
faq.answer: No. Paying twice a month gives 24 half-payments a year, the same as 12 monthly payments. Paying every two weeks gives 26 half-payments, which is one extra full payment a year and is where the savings come from.

faq.question: Does paying biweekly lower my interest rate?
faq.answer: No. The rate stays the same. You pay less total interest only because the balance falls faster, so there is less principal left to charge interest on.

faq.question: Can I switch to biweekly payments partway through my loan?
faq.answer: Usually yes, if your servicer allows it. Enter the years already paid under More options to see the effect from your current balance. The later you start, the smaller the savings, because less interest is left to save.

faq.question: Are biweekly mortgage programs worth the fees?
faq.answer: Compare the fees with the savings after fees shown above. Because you can get almost the same result by adding one-twelfth of a payment each month at no cost, a paid program mainly offers convenience.

faq.question: Will biweekly payments help me drop PMI sooner?
faq.answer: They can. Conventional PMI is based on the loan balance compared with the original home value, so paying principal down faster reaches the cancellation point earlier. Your servicer decides when the requirement is met.
